node: Sulphur and sulphuric-acid feedstock for copper SX-EW and nickel HPAL
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe around the sulphur/sulphuric-acid feedstock chokepoint with emphasis on underfollowed second-order exposures rather than obvious copper/nickel megacaps. The strongest direct small/mid-cap mapping found in this pass is Taseko Mines, because its Florence Copper SX-EW ramp is directly acid-linked and management has disclosed a fixed-price sulphuric-acid contract for 2026. Kirby is a weaker but potentially underappreciated logistics derivative: it is not proven to be an acid-specific beneficiary, but its US tank-barge network sits in the liquid chemical and agricultural-chemical transport layer that could matter if trade routes reroute. Teck is included as a reference/large-cap context name because Trail produces chemical/fertilizer products and has documented sulphur capture into sulphuric acid, but its market cap is above the preferred discovery range. Mosaic is an adjacent fertilizer-sector signal and possible pricing/cost transmission candidate: sulphur price stress has already driven production curtailments, making it relevant for cross-sector competition for sulphur/acid even though it is not a copper/nickel producer.
